title: Improvising and habit
summary: Most improvising is habit, even for real talents.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: A lot of people call it improvising, but it's not necessarily so. I think that probably is the enticement behind the contact of improvising, but that alone to me is not enough. It almost requires constant repetition in order to achieve, occasionally, something that you haven't done before. You have to do mostly what you have been doing. It's not as free as critics
There are too many people who think they're improvisors who to me are pattern players. They're not really improvising, they're giving back to you what they've--
Whatever is their habit. It becomes a habit.
A talent, a real talent, will always still do this. Ninety percent of what a real talent does is habit, but his habits then may be more perceptive.

Occasionally also, if he has allowed himself to develop in that way, will do something that he is not aware that he has done until after he has done it, and then it becomes part of his habit. But that's for him; he's found that and he really can't do that to anyone else.
I've always been leery of methods, and yet you have to have something, when you're beginning particularly, something

to latch onto. But I've seen so many people get on the thing and it's false and they re- tain this falseness all their lives, or they spend an inordinate amount of effort to try to get rid of it, without really knowing what they're trying to get in its place. That's the responsibility of a teacher that overwhelms me.
That didn't have much to do with Benny; did it?
Who cares? It has to do with you and that's what we're talking about.
